svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.25.2.4 Installation of Loose-Fill Insulation
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.25 HEAT TRANSFER, AIR LEAKAGE AND CONDENSATION CONTROL
Installation of Loose-Fill Insulation

g.text: Supporting slope not more than 4.5 in 12 for mineral
or cellulose fibre and 2.5 in 12 for other types, (2)
Soffit vents kept clear and air path kept
between the outer and inner wythes of

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Except as provided in Sentences (2) to (6), loose-fill
insulation is used on horizontal surfaces only.
Where loose-fill insulation is installed in an unconfined
sloped space, such as an attic space over a sloped ceiling,
the supporting slope is not more than
(a) 4.5 in 12 for mineral fibre or cellulose fibre insulation, and
(b) 2.5 in 12 for other types of insulation.
Loose-fill insulation is permitted to be used in wood-frame
walls of existing buildings. (See Note A-9.25.2.4.(3).)
Where blown-in insulation is installed in above-ground or
below-ground wood-frame walls of new buildings,
(a) the density of the installed insulation is sufficient to
preclude settlement, (b) the insulation is installed behind a
membrane that will permit visual inspection prior to the
installation of the interior finish, (c) the insulation is
installed in a manner that will not interfere with the installation
of the interior finish, and (d) no water is added to the
insulation, unless it can be shown that the added water will not
adversely affect other materials in the assembly.
Water repellent loose-fill insulation is permitted to be used
between the outer and inner wythes of masonry cavity walls.
Where soffit venting is used, measures are taken
(a) to prevent loose-fill insulation from blocking the soffit vents
and to maintain an open path for circulation of air from the vents
into the attic or roof space, and (b) to minimize airflow into the
insulation near the soffit vents to maintain the thermal
performance of the material. (See Article 9.19.1.3.)
Drawn: B at a slope of 4.5 in 12. D shows a baffle over the insulation at the eave, one way to meet (6). Sizes are illustration only.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.25.2.4. (page 9-233)
